The estate can recover damages for the pedestrian's initial injuries, but the driver is generally not liable for the death because her refusal of life-saving treatment was a superseding cause breaking the chain of causation. Under the contributory negligence rule noted, her negligent refusal would bar all recovery, though in a comparative-fault jurisdiction recovery would merely be reduced. Thus, absent a jurisdiction applying contributory negligence, recovery is limited to damages attributable to the original negligence before the refusal.

CONFIDENCE: 80
